title: The voucher has a minimum
hook: A €5 voucher can leave a small basket unchanged.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Apply a discontinuous minimum-purchase rule accurately.

misconception: Every basket gets the advertised voucher deduction.
objective: Apply a discontinuous minimum-purchase rule accurately.

claims.text: A fictional voucher subtracts €5 only when the basket is at least €30. Scaled model; fictional rule; €30 qualifying minimum.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Basket=28€, A=€28 and B=€28. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A="x"; B=["-","x",["*",5,["floor",["min",1,["/","x",30]]]]]; x denotes Basket. At x=28, A=28, B=28; recall at x=31: B=26. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions.

claims.text: The threshold is part of the rule. Below €30 the deduction is zero; at €30 it becomes €5. An advertised deduction cannot be applied before checking eligibility.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: A fictional voucher subtracts €5 only when the basket is at least €30. Change only Basket to 31€. What is B (Voucher) now? Correct: €26. Use B's stated rule with Basket=31€: it gives €26. The threshold is part of the rule. Below €30 the deduction is zero; at €30 it becomes €5. An advertised deduction cannot be applied before checking eligibility.
